title: How Steve Jobs ran Pixar: no contracts, inverted hierarchy, and stories that outlast technology
summary: In a 1996 interview Jobs explains his role at Pixar as creating the environment where top creative and technical talent can do their best work, why Pixar avoids contracts, and why storytelling, not technology, makes films last. Two short emails show him persuading a team to join the holiday waltz and announcing Apple's acquisition of NeXT.

principles.text: A leader's job is to build the environment where brilliant people can do their best work, not to do the creative work himself.
principles.quote: What I try to do is help create the environment where all these incredible people can make films.

principles.text: Retain great people by making the company so good they never want to leave, not by locking them in with contracts.
principles.quote: Every single day we worry about how we can make Pixar a better company so that nobody will ever want to leave, and so we don't take anybody for granted.

principles.text: With rare, in-demand talent, the hierarchy inverts: management exists to support the people doing the front-line work.
principles.quote: the hierarchy of power sort of inverts, and the CEO is actually at the bottom. I sort of feel like I work for most of these people because they're the ones that are doing all the brilliant work.

principles.text: Stay intensely focused on one thing: building a great feature animation studio.
principles.quote: What we're doing is just a pure play to build a feature animation studio.

principles.text: Technology can't rescue a weak story; storytelling is an old art that technology doesn't change.
principles.quote: no amount of technology can turn a bad story into a good story.

principles.text: Products built on technology fade quickly, but great stories renew themselves across generations, and creating them is a privilege.
principles.quote: people are going to be watching Toy Story in sixty years. Not because of the computer graphics, but because of the story about friendship.
